citeturn17search3 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: today; ES/cancelled SKUs (`222b` 3090 ES, `222f` 3080 11/12GB ES, `2205`, `2207`) are GA102 cores inside the span and run as-is for anyone holding one; tier 🟢 (upstream silicon) until a first hardware report. ... No marker; after Enter the whole chain is green: scrubber incomplete but proceeding (community shape), FWSEC WPR2 verified, booter `payload_mode=true`, selectors read back, POST-FLR AON survival, native-GOP rebuilt 1920x1080 with `display path verified`, BME restored, handoff, Windows booted with no problem code.
2026-11-02 pci.ids correction: the old "3070 Ti 2205" entry was wrong - the shipping 3070 Ti is GA104 `2482`, while `2205` / `2207` are cancelled GA102 ES SKUs (RTX 3080 Ti 20GB / a GA102 3070 Ti), now listed explicitly as ES above. The runtime span is narrowed to `0x2200..=0x223f` accordingly (the old 0x22..ff tail holds no GA102 cores - only HD-audio functions, Tegra/THOR/GB10 ARM blocks and H100 NVSwitch). ES/cancelled SKUs (`222b` 3090 ES, `222f` 3080 11/12GB ES, `2205`, `2207`) are GA102 cores inside the span and run as-is for anyone holding one; tier 🟢 (upstream silicon) until a first hardware report. Sources: #29, #15.

`2203` first complete log + output-hash A/B (#195, 2026-11-06): MSI 3090 Ti, Gigabyte X570 GAMING X (AMI F38f), 5950X, Windows 11 26200, driver 616.92, 480 W stock; Above 4G/ReBAR on (BAR1 256 -> 32768 MiB), CSM off, no mods. No marker; after Enter the whole chain is green: scrubber incomplete but proceeding (community shape), FWSEC WPR2 verified, booter `payload_mode=true`, selectors read back, POST-FLR AON survival, native-GOP rebuilt 1920x1080 with `display path verified`, BME restored, handoff, Windows booted with no problem code. In-OS ssdiag was not run (limit), but the unlocked state is self-evident from the A/B: FP16 71.5 -> 99.5, BF16 72.6 -> 120.4, TF32 36.1 -> 64.1, FP32 control flat at 25.4, per-mode output SHA-256 identical; power stays in the same band and is slightly lower unlocked (FP16 467 -> 446 W) while clocks fall 1950 -> 1800, the power-wall shape. TF32 doubles on this card too (1.77x), same direction as #194. Note: `-Out G:\` trips a PS 5.1 `New-Item` illegal-path error (fixed, see FAQ); the first round hit the 30 s timeout with zero writes. Evidence in `docs/evidence/issue195-2203-x570/`.
